question: Which of the following Sun temples is built by Raja Bhimdev I of the Solanki dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Modhera Sun Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Modhera Sun Temple was built by **Raja Bhimdev I** of the Solanki dynasty in the early 11th century (circa 1026 CE).
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Surya, the Sun God**, and is located in the village of Modhera, Gujarat, India.
 
• The temple is renowned for its **intricate carvings**, architectural precision, and unique alignment with the equinox, allowing sunlight to illuminate the sanctum sanctorum.
 
• The Modhera Sun Temple is considered a prime example of the **Maru-Gurjara architectural style**.
 
• Though no worship is conducted there today, the temple is a protected monument under the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sun Temples in India**

 
 
• Other famous Sun Temples in India include the **Konark Sun Temple** in Odisha and the **Martand Sun Temple** in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• These temples are dedicated to Surya, symbolizing energy, vitality, and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Style**
 
 
• The Maru-Gurjara style, prominent in western India, emphasizes ornate carvings, stepped tanks, and open-air courtyards.
 
• The Modhera Sun Temple exemplifies this style with its **assembly hall (Sabha Mandap), sanctum (Garbhagriha), and stepped reservoir (Kunda)**.
 
 
 
• **Alignment with the Sun**
 
 
• The temple's sanctum is designed in such a way that during the equinox, the first rays of the sun illuminate the idol of Surya.
 
• This alignment reflects the advanced astronomical knowledge of the era.
 
 
 
• **Solanki Dynasty**
 
 
• The Solanki dynasty, also known as the Chaulukya dynasty, ruled parts of present-day Gujarat and Rajasthan between the 10th and 13th centuries.
 
• They were great patrons of art and architecture, as evidenced by monuments like the Modhera Sun Temple and the Rani ki Vav stepwell.
